turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'll be direct. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me, and why did Owen find out from his phone in the middle of class?
Thanks for coming in. The zero went in before I called you, and that was wrong.
Okay. Then take it out of the gradebook today. And before you say another word about the essay, tell me what you have besides a score.
I will remove the zero tomorrow morning. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch on Thursday. Nothing goes on his record. I will put all of that in an email to you tonight.
I'm writing down tomorrow morning. But you're asking my son to redo the work, so what exactly are you saying he has to prove, and on what basis?
Yes, all of it, in writing tonight.
The email is fine, but that wasn't my question. What else do you have, Hale, that makes a rewrite necessary?
Okay, I think that is the end of the meeting. Thank you.
We're not finished. You still haven't told me what the rewrite is for, and I'm not leaving until you do.
